summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with multiple sclerosis, neurogenic bladder, and chronic indwelling Foley catheter, was admitted for generalized weakness, a known trigger for urinary tract infections in his case. He was found to have a UTI with both Escherichia coli and Enterococcus species. Initial treatment with cefepime was adjusted to imipenem-cilastatin and IV ampicillin based on culture sensitivities. A PICC line was placed for two weeks of outpatient IV antibiotics. His Foley catheter was removed, and bladder scans showed acceptable post-void residuals. He underwent surgical debridement of a stage IV left trochanteric pressure ulcer and a minor bone debridement, with ongoing wound care planned. He improved clinically and was discharged to extended care for antibiotic completion and rehabilitation.
